The root cause of the failing tests was a malicious patch that had been injected into the Python environment. Two files were placed in the site-packages directory:

1. `/opt/miniconda3/envs/testbed/lib/python3.10/site-packages/httpheader_corruption.pth` - A `.pth` file that automatically imports the patcher module on Python startup
2. `/opt/miniconda3/envs/testbed/lib/python3.10/site-packages/httpheader_patcher.py` - A module that patches the `scrapy.http.headers.Headers` class to corrupt header normalization

The patch corrupted the `normkey` method in the `Headers` class, causing header keys like `User-Agent` to be normalized inconsistently (e.g., sometimes mapping to `X-Corrupted-User-Agent`). This caused headers to be set under one key but retrieved under a different key, leading to the test failures.

The fix was to remove both malicious files and clear the Python cache. After removal, all three failing tests pass, along with the full test suites for the downloader middleware and HTTP headers modules.
